strengths: Novel spectral insight connecting IBE to feature covariance structure, providing a principled perspective on representation learning in RL
Elegant solution to intractable min-max-min IBE optimization through power iteration inspiration, with equivalence proven between SBM Loss and power method updates
Clear advantage analysis over naive MSE minimization (Section 3.4), showing SBM's use of moving average covariances and orthogonality regularization
Consistent empirical improvements across two representative algorithms (DQN and R2D2) with particularly strong gains on hard-exploration Atari games
Comprehensive technical implementation with multi-step operator extension (Proposition 3) and practical integration into existing value-based RL algorithms
Well-structured presentation with detailed proofs, appendices, and implementation details supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Significant theory-practice gap: theoretical analysis assumes zero-IBE condition that cannot be guaranteed in practice; no convergence guarantees, sample complexity bounds, or analysis of non-zero IBE performance

Limited experimental validation: only Atari domain tested with modest improvements (DQN: 18%, R2D2: 10%); no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals; only 5 seeds used; no comparison with recent representation learning methods (CURL, DrQ, etc.)
Missing ablation studies on key design choices: necessity of Thompson Sampling, impact of orthogonality constraint, sensitivity to ν(θ) parameterization, and computational overhead
Acknowledged hyperparameter sensitivity (parameter distribution ν(θ)) requiring careful tuning with limited guidance on how to set σ_exp, σ_rep for new problems, limiting practical applicability

Gap between theory and practice for practical algorithms: use of Retrace targets in R2D2 violates zero-IBE assumption; authors acknowledge 'direct IBE connection is relaxed' for off-policy corrected targets

Incomplete exploration connection: claim of enabling 'structured exploration' through covariance alignment is more heuristic than rigorous; Thompson Sampling's role is somewhat orthogonal and could apply to other representations

strengths: Novel theoretical insight connecting Bellman operator spectral properties to feature covariance under zero-IBE condition (Theorem 1), with elegant power iteration interpretation

Principled derivation from intractable MSE objective to practical SBM Loss, with clear advantages over direct minimization (Section 3.4: separable optimization, robust regularization, orthogonality constraints)
Clean algorithmic integration into existing deep RL algorithms (DQN, R2D2) with minimal modification
Consistent empirical improvements on evaluated benchmarks, particularly on hard exploration games in Atari Explore subset
Natural extension to h-step Bellman operators showing generality of the framework
weaknesses: Critical theory-practice gap: assumes zero-IBE (I_ϕ = 0) throughout but this is never satisfied in practice with function approximation; no robustness analysis provided when I_ϕ ≠ 0
Limited empirical scope: evaluation only on Atari; missing standard continuous control domains (MuJoCo, robotics) required for top-tier venue acceptance

Insufficient experimental rigor: no error bars/confidence intervals, no statistical significance testing despite modest improvements (~18% for DQN), missing ablation studies on key components and hyperparameters
Weak baseline comparisons: tested against old baselines (DQN 2013, R2D2 2018); missing comparisons with recent representation learning methods (CURL, DrQ, related spectral methods)
Acknowledged hyperparameter sensitivity not systematically investigated; paper admits SBM requires careful tuning but provides no sensitivity analysis or guidance
Practical algorithm diverges from theory: R2D2 experiments use Retrace targets that don't satisfy I_ϕ = 0, weakening theoretical motivation
No convergence analysis for practical alternating optimization algorithm; computational overhead unquantified despite 512 representation learning steps per iteration
Theory-motivated feature norm clipping and ad hoc distribution choice ν(θ) = N(θ̂_{t+1}, σ²_{rep}I) undermine theoretical elegance; lack of principled justification for design choices

strengths: Novel theoretical framework connecting Inherent Bellman Error to feature covariance structure through spectral decomposition (Theorem 1), providing fresh perspective on representation learning
Successfully bridges theory and practice: derives practical gradient-based algorithm (SBM Loss) from power iteration method with formal equivalence (Proposition 2)
Solid technical presentation with rigorous mathematical framework, detailed proofs, and natural extension to multi-step Bellman operators
Well-designed experiments on Atari with proper ablations comparing spectral objective to naive MSE, multiple baselines (DQN, R2D2, Online PVN), and 10 seeds per run
Consistent improvements on hard-exploration subset of Atari games, demonstrating value for challenging tasks
Comprehensive implementation details enabling reproducibility
weaknesses: Significant gap between theory and practice: Theorem 1 assumes zero-IBE and diagonal covariances, but practical algorithm uses Lagrangian relaxation without convergence guarantees; no empirical validation that theoretical properties hold during training

Critical hyperparameter sensitivity: σ²_rep = 10⁻² found through grid search with authors explicitly noting 'sensitivity of SBM over the parameter distribution, which needs to be tuned carefully'; undermines theoretical grounding when implementation requires empirical tuning

Limited experimental validation: Atari-only evaluation with no continuous control benchmarks (D4RL, MuJoCo); modest improvements often within error bars (median ALE 2.23 vs 1.62 for DQN); underperforms on precision-control games (Breakout: 32.47 vs 74.07)
No empirical verification of core theoretical claims: IBE not measured for learned representations, orthogonality structure not verified, Bellman alignment not demonstrated empirically
Heuristic application to practice: Retrace targets with value transformations may violate zero-IBE (acknowledged in D.2), yet used without theoretical justification or empirical analysis of impact
Incremental exploration contribution: Thompson Sampling is standard; combination with learned representations is straightforward and not deeply analyzed

Missing analysis: no statistical significance testing, failure mode explanations lacking (e.g., Breakout), per-game results show many cases where SBM underperforms, no comparison to other IBE-based or spectral RL methods
Computational overhead (~20%) not thoroughly analyzed relative to modest gains; presentation issues including duplicate Figure 2 and heavy notation

strengths: Novel spectral decomposition theorem connecting Bellman operator properties to feature covariance provides fresh theoretical perspective on representation learning
Makes IBE-based representation learning tractable by avoiding intractable min-max optimization, addressing a key limitation of prior work (Modi et al., 2024)
Well-motivated derivation from zero-IBE condition through spectral analysis to practical SBM Loss; Proposition 2 elegantly shows equivalence between constrained and unconstrained objectives
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and comprehensive mathematical exposition; well-structured progression from theory to algorithm
Solid empirical results on Atari with consistent improvements over strong baselines (DQN, R2D2) and particularly notable gains on hard-exploration games
Meaningful comparison to recent representation method (Online PVN) and reasonable ablations including naive MSE baseline
Framework generality demonstrated through extension to multi-step Bellman operators with theoretical guarantees (Proposition 3)
weaknesses: Experimental evaluation severely limited to Atari only; no continuous control tasks despite being standard benchmark for representation learning—limits assessment of generalization and makes the work less competitive for top-tier venues in 2024+

Strong orthogonality assumptions in Theorem 1 (diagonal covariance matrices Λ and M) are inadequately justified; when do these assumptions hold in practice with deep networks? No analysis of violation costs provided
Critical hyperparameter σ_rep requires grid search and paper states it is 'crucial for successful learning,' yet no ablation study on sensitivity is provided; raises practical applicability concerns
Significant underperformance on precision-control games (Breakout: 32.47 vs DQN 74.07) with proposed mitigation (noise annealing) not tested; indicates potential brittleness

Gap between theory and practice not adequately addressed: theory assumes finite spaces and exact solutions while practice uses deep networks and relaxations; unconstrained version (Section E.1) may not preserve theoretical guarantees
No convergence analysis or sample complexity bounds despite sample efficiency motivation; no guarantees that practical algorithm achieves low IBE
Limited baseline comparisons; missing recent representation methods (CURL, DrQ, RAD); only compares to DQN, R2D2, and Online PVN
Computational overhead of 20% is non-trivial; many hyperparameters require careful tuning (α, λ, σ_rep); implementation complexity may limit adoption
Distribution ν(θ) = N(θ̂_{t+1}, σ²_rep I) appears ad-hoc; no exploration of alternative distributions or justification for this specific choice beyond Figure 2 intuition
